notes: THE BIGGEST FINDING — the Card-1 coupling trio is STRUCTURALLY INERT under Card 4. src/core/app/ApplicationNetworkAssembly.cpp:1533-1534 reads `const bool do_amb_carry = (phase_datum_prioritized || !st.is_pivot) && !carry_invariant;` and the only two `cb.buildCplRow` call sites are inside that loop (:1572) and the `zwd_on` block (:1603). network.carry_zwd is false by default and set in ZERO shipped configs. So with carry_invariant=true (the production posture, 208 configs), carry_conditional_coupling / _time_update / _joint_whiten / _sh_marginalize fold NOTHING, while shared_carry_full_cov's dense block silently shrinks to Clock+CodeBias (PhaseBias is skipped at NetworkRunContext.cpp:~1697). All four coupling knobs are nevertheless set true in 200+ configs. The post-solve harvest still runs, so the run-end 'coupling-carry volume' line shows stashes>0 with injected terms 0 — a half-healthy log. This retro-explains the hr-4 'exoneration' of carry_coupling_time_update (off -> 54.3/118.3, bit-identical): the Card-1e lesson ('a byte-identical A/B usually means the feature NEVER RAN') applies to that reading.

SECOND FINDING — network.carry_invariant_honesty is PARSED-INERT with NO warning. Verified with two tools per the standing directive: networkCarryInvariantHonesty() is called at exactly one site, the run-manifest writer src/core/logging/NetworkRunTraces.cpp:880. 166 shipped configs set it true and the carry_invariant ON summary prints 'honesty=true' (GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:2835) as if the instrument were live. Unlike innov_refold there is no inert-warning. Nothing was ever measured by it.

The promotion-ready core is a PACKAGE, not four independent knobs: phase_datum_eq34 + carry_invariant + carry_invariant_qz=1e-4 + carry_invariant_innov_gate + carry_invariant_innov_calibrate. Splitting it is unsafe in both directions — eq34 WITHOUT carry_invariant measured ~100x worse than the legacy pivot datum (76.2 vs 0.085 cyc/ep), and carry_invariant with q_z=0 and NO innovation gate is a stiff zero-q carry with no event response, which standing invariant #1 forbids. The loader already fail-louds two of the three edges (carry_invariant requires eq34; innov_gate requires carry_invariant; innov_calibrate requires innov_gate) but does NOT enforce 'q_z==0 requires innov_gate'.

Cross-scale caution that mirrors the mw_wl.bridge_sample_debias counterexample: the ONE knob in this family with a measured 50-vs-305 inversion is state_snapshot_carry_diagonal, and the inversion is CONSTELLATION-keyed, not station-count-keyed — GPS-only 305 says diag >= dense, GPS+Galileo 305 says warm-diagonal is worse than cold (3.3x D5 re-tap churn, 91 m CLK spike). Treat 'validated GPS-only' as a genuine scope boundary for every snapshot knob.

Grading-method constraints that any promotion run must respect, all paid for already: (1) grade only datum-invariant quantities — total_IF(sat) = CLK + 2.545728*CB(sat,C1W) - 1.545728*CB(sat,C2W) as a deviation from the per-epoch median over ALL sats INCLUDING the pivot; rms_clock_m (NetworkStashStatus.cpp:149-155) is RMS about zero of the RAW clock state and is an invariant-#5 violation. (2) At 305 sta judge hourly LEVEL BANDS, never slopes — a restored diagonal P makes ep20 a local minimum ~30% below the true floor. (3) Never compare formal sigma across arms without the calibration ratio (control sigma=0.26 with calib 22.3x vs Card-4 calib 0.49). (4) 6h windows covering 04:00 UTC are the standard discriminator length on DOY-129 — every 3h grading window sits just short of the hr-4 cliff.

Perf scope for any 'turn it on' decision: the Card-4 carry pipeline is 56.8% of a 27.72 s/epoch 305-station all-on run (fold 34.5% incl. an 11.0% serial KxK Cholesky). carry_invariant is therefore the single most expensive knob in this family; shared_carry_full_cov measured ~free at 50 sta (859 vs 858 ms/ep) and carry_coupling_joint_whiten ~1% (439.2 vs 434.7 ms/ep). 1 s cadence at 305 sta is unreachable by optimization with this carry armed.

Not audited here because their defaults are non-zero: carry_invariant_emit_rebase (GnssConfig.hpp:4782, default TRUE — the only default-ON knob in the family; it is what emit_pb_filter and the PB gate v2 hang off), carry_invariant_innov_calibrate_window (60.0), carry_vce_components ('pl'), carry_vce_window_epochs (60), state_snapshot_interval_s (10.0). state_snapshot_interval_s is inert without state_snapshot_path and is clamped to 10.0 if <= 0 (GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:669-672).

THE PROMOTION CANDIDATE IN THIS FAMILY IS EXACTLY ONE: network.station_pd_pin_aware. It is the only knob here with a single-variable A/B at TWO scales (50 and 305 stations), an unambiguous mechanism, no measured counter-scope, and a loader that already prints a RECOMMEND line for it. Everything else in the family is scoped, falsified, or unmeasured.

THE SECOND TIER IS A BUNDLE, NOT A KNOB: phase_datum_eq34 + carry_invariant + code_datum_time_linked + station_pd_pin_aware + estimate_iono_sh/estimate_sat_code_bias is the de-facto working default already (211/217 and 245/245 of configs that mention eq34 / code_datum_time_linked set them true; both 305-sta flagships carry all five). The audit finding is that the shipped DEFAULTS have drifted far from the working configuration — but the bundle must move together. eq34 alone is ~100x worse than the legacy pivot datum on DD-step, so promoting eq34 without carry_invariant would be a regression.

BLAST RADIUS WARNING — network.service_mode force-arms a measured NO-GO. armBool(network_clock_model_) at GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:3062 turns on the two-state oscillator that project_clock_model_hadamard_calib.md closed with data (measured noise-type slope p ~ 1.0, i.e. no RWFM anywhere; the shipped q2=1.5e-7 is 17x above the emitted-clock upper bound and 4-6 orders above the intrinsic one). Any real-time service run today silently ships that. This is the single highest-value fix in the family and it is a DEFAULT-MEMBERSHIP question, not a knob question.

THREE MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE GAUGE FAMILIES, ENFORCED DIFFERENTLY — worth knowing before writing any config: clock gauge = {pivot pin (default) | clock_datum_sum_to_zero | clock_datum_broadcast_anchored}, the latter two hard-error together; phase gauge = {clock-pivot station (default) | phase_datum_prioritized | phase_datum_ensemble | phase_datum_eq34}, where eq34+ensemble hard-error and eq34 SILENTLY supersedes prioritized (log-only); code IF-pin retarget = {code_datum_time_linked | clock_signal_basis_hold}, which THROW a std::runtime_error together rather than returning a load error.

SILENT SIDE EFFECTS TO CHECK IN THE LOG, NOT THE JSON: (a) estimate_iono_sh force-enables estimate_sat_code_bias, which in turn force-DISABLES model_corrections.enable_code_phase_bias — a config that writes .BIA=true still runs false (this is how phantom .BIA coverage got in); (b) network.clock_model makes filter.sat_clock_q a byte-identical no-op; (c) network.clock_model makes network.emit_clock_rate inert while the load log still claims emit_clock_rate is the active mechanism; (d) clock_datum_sum_to_zero / broadcast_anchored make sticky_pivot and pivot_vanish_return_signal inert and silently ignore clock_datum_satellite; (e) carry_invariant makes eq34_pin_round / carry_shift / rpb_q inert; (f) filter.process_noise.clock_bias_q is INERT ON THE NETWORK PRODUCER - the per-station receiver clock is a per-epoch LOCAL parameter (estimated fresh, marginalized, never carried), so a process-noise value for it has nothing to act on: runs/golden_sim_campaign_zwdblk_rxq (clock_bias_q 1000 -> 0.09 on the in-block posture) has products.txt sha256 bba9a7f2865070bc... BYTE-IDENTICAL to its control and a T4 run-end counter identical to the digit, with no warning anywhere.  The knob is meaningful on the PPP / baseline / real-time paths only.  What it would have modelled is real - the simulator's own receiver-clock truth is a deterministic drift plus a WHITE increment (mean step +2.997e-08 s / 30 s ~ +0.2995 m/s, step sd 1.0055e-09 s = 0.301 m, second-difference sd 1.436e-09 s = sqrt(2)x that) - so the honest RW carry is a CARD, not a knob: network.carry_rx_clock_in_block, the ZWD card's sibling inside the F3 block (SPEC_amb_iono_split_overcount s6.19d, s7 item 42), whose one design risk is that a plain RW on the ABSOLUTE clock fights a 9 m/epoch ramp three decades above the increment it models.

THE 'MEASURED AT ONE SCALE' TRAP APPEARS TWICE HERE, in the same shape as the mw_wl.bridge_sample_debias counterexample. estimate_glonass: 3-station fixture PASSES (121/121, datum dim 3) and an 11-epoch 305-sta smoke looks clean at 2.6 m rms, but the 1-hour 305-sta run collapses the entire Galileo clock block 38 minutes in (E14 -12.4 km) with the rank gate reporting gate_ok=1 throughout. estimate_sat_code_bias: 3-sta closed loop 0.508 m (drop-in for .BIA) but 50-sta FULL consumption gives 129-270 m and the 150-sta/3h OSB correlation stalls at hour 1.2. Neither can be promoted on its passing scale.

GRADING DISCIPLINE THAT INVALIDATES SOME EXISTING 'EVIDENCE' IN THIS FAMILY: rms_clock_m (NetworkStashStatus.cpp:149-155) is RMS about zero of the RAW clock state — datum-dependent, so any datum A/B graded on it is a standing-invariant-#5 violation. The valid quantity is total_IF(sat) = CLK + 2.545728*CB(sat,C1W) - 1.545728*CB(sat,C2W) as a deviation from the per-epoch median over ALL satellites INCLUDING the pivot. Also: sigma0_pf is identically zero on phase rows when phase_leveling is off — read sigma0_pf_code, never the pooled sigma0_pf.

NOT CLASSIFIED (defaults are non-zero, listed for interlock completeness): phase_datum_eq34_pin_round defaults TRUE at :2045 but is force-INERT under carry_invariant, i.e. it is on-by-default and never runs in the recommended regime; phase_datum_eq34_rpb_prior_sigma_m defaults 1.0 and is recorded as 'the rank floor that cures W5 withholds' (78 withholds -> 0); phase_datum_eq34_rpb_q_m2s defaults 3e-6 and is INERT under carry_invariant; phase_datum_sticky defaults true; phase_datum_pref_elev_deg defaults 15.0 (recorded as load-bearing); rank_gate_tol defaults 1e-9 and is explicitly PER-CONFIG ('Never edit it globally' — a value below a healthy config's gauge depth withholds that healthy config); clock_model_q2 1.5e-7 / k_sigma 6.0 / meas_std_m 0.05 are all falsified-by-calibration values inherited from the NO-GO card.

ADJACENT KNOBS I DID NOT CLASSIFY BUT THAT GATE THIS FAMILY'S RECOMMENDATIONS: network.cb_admission (:857, false), network.cb_kaula_prior (:2216ish, false) and network.rank_gate_tol (:2233, 1e-9) form the 4-piece chain that is the ONLY way estimate_sat_code_bias emits with BeiDou in the roster ('Each piece is NECESSARY; none alone emits' — 305-sta storm arm goes 0 -> 6/6 dumps emitted). PROMOTION VERDICT for this family: exactly ONE knob is unambiguously promotable — network.estimate_iono_sh, which is already a standing user directive ("ALWAYS on") and is set in 224 configs, yet still ships default-false at GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:794-795. The next two biggest promotion gaps are NUMERIC defaults, not toggles: estimation.ionosphere_weighting.elevation_cutoff_deg ships 10.0 while every field config uses 25.0 (measured 77x clock-delta rms penalty), and estimation.global_vtec_sh.max_degree ships 4 while field configs use 15 (305-sta) or 8 (50-sta GPS tri). Those two are where accidental re-discovery actually happens.

The two Iono-2 knobs (layer2_max_degree, rep_error_tau_s) are the clearest case of 'validated-good' NOT applying: both are BUILT, gated, byte-identity-clean, counter-live, committed — and both have only a 60-epoch A/B that returned statistical parity BY DESIGN (tau=900 s is ~2 time constants in 30 min). They are UNVALIDATED, not validated-good-but-off. One 3 h+ 50-sta run with arms {off, A, B, A+B} settles both; graded on per-signal NL circR, DD step vs the ~2 cyc/ep shared-param floor, and carry_vce calibration ~1.

The mwwl bridge_sample_debias counterexample has a direct analogue here: network.iono_constraint_deweight_adaptive is armed in 181 configs on the strength of a 305-station AMPUTATION experiment, but the gate ITSELF has never been A/B'd, and the one 305-station 24 h run that instrumented it found it engaging 174 distinct stations (peak 72 simultaneous) against a 2-station design target. Arming breadth is not validation. Treat 'it is on in all the configs' as evidence of drift, not evidence of benefit.

DEFAULTS IN THIS FAMILY THAT ARE ALREADY CORRECT — do not touch: global_vtec_sh.sun_fixed=true (GnssConfigLoad.cpp:1318-1319; no config overrides it, and CV/rate modelling is explicitly NOT a lever for a sun-fixed field because the frame removes the ramp); representation_sigma_tecu=5.0 (:1315-1317) — the free-iono discriminator sigma_rep=50 collapsed LOS>3sigma 0.785->0.025 yet DD fractions stayed uniform, and 'sigma_rep = 50 is not an operating point (it also kills GF/DCB separation over long windows)'; ionosphere_weighting.floor_m=0.05 and the other floors (:1280-1281) — the floors-divided-by-10 arm DIVERGED at 12 h in both pin regimes (a00 -> 4012 / 798->1478, 11-13 cyc/ep), and divergence there is 'floor-driven, pin-independent'; ionosphere_weighting.common_mode_sigma_m=50.0 (:1275-1277) is structural (it is what leaves the receiver-DCB<->iono level free); mean_vtec_prior 15 +/- 30 must stay LOOSE (the tight anchor belongs on layer 2, whose a00 split is quasi-null).

LOADER FORCING / FAIL-LOUD MAP for this family (matters for how anything here can be recommended): estimate_iono_sh forces six other flags on and two off (GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:796-799, 817-840) — it is 'the SINGLE arm' for the whole W6 bias slice, so it can never be A/B'd in isolation; apriori_source=brdc_rts + estimate_sat_code_bias without estimate_iono_sh is a HARD ERROR return-false (:951-960); rep_error_tau_s>0 silently zeroes row_decimation_epochs (GnssConfigLoad.cpp:1393); sh_health_gate silently self-disables without estimate_iono_sh or with no active condition (:1665-1675); cb_admission armed without the W6 slice warns INERT (:882-886).

SCOPE CORRECTION worth recording, because two memory records disagree and the newer data wins: the 'estimate_iono_sh observability floor' (GPS-only withholds EVERY epoch) was measured on a 50-station 7-config smoke. It does NOT hold at scale with genuine triple-frequency data — 79 repo configs are GPS-only with estimate_iono_sh true, and the Jul-17 GPS-only tri-freq bench ran 60 ep with 0 withheld and SH deg-8 fully observable. The real prerequisite is >=3 frequencies PRESENT IN THE DATA (the 'L5 in the RINEX header != L5 in the data' trap: GLPS/TWTF/WUHN declare L5Q and carry zero L5), plus frequency_mode/channel_mode 'all' at multi-constellation. Anyone re-reading the old floor statement will wrongly conclude GPS-only is unusable.

Nothing in this family is KEEP_OFF because it was FALSIFIED except network.sh_health_gate (a00 band non-transferable, degrade path deadlocked) and the adaptive_iono_process_noise cluster (structurally inert on the network/RT paths). ★ SINGLE BIGGEST FINDING — the whole RAIM family is structurally INERT on most of the config fleet. ApplicationNetwork.cpp:1577 gates post-fit RAIM on `raim_on && carry_warm`, and NetworkSolveGlue.cpp:734 gates the within-epoch tier on `within_epoch_armed && carry_warm`, where carry_warm = pl_on && ... (ApplicationNetwork.cpp:1117; pl_on = networkPhaseLeveling(), NetworkRunContext.cpp:44). I counted 173 of 335 network configs running carry_invariant with phase_leveling=false. On every one of them, arming network.raim / raim_attribution / raim_within_epoch / raim_withhold_sigma0 / per_const_withhold / raim_we_code_iono changes NOTHING and no warning is logged. This is exactly standing invariant #4 (clean log, dead wiring). feedback_raim_always_on.md already flags decoupling sigma0_adapt from carry_warm as sanctioned-but-unbuilt; until it is built, 'RAIM always on' is unachievable on the Card-4 lineage. Any promotion of a RAIM knob should be paired with a loader WARN when raim* is armed with phase_leveling off.

★ ORDERING: post-fit RAIM, attribution and the clock monitor all run AFTER emit (driver order SolveGlue 1488 -> InstallCarry 1522 -> SolPrep 1535 -> EmitStore 1546 -> RAIM 1577 -> ClockQc 1585). project_network_ssystem_dia_assessment.md item 4: 'exactly one contaminated epoch ships unflagged'. So network.raim is next-epoch protection; only raim_within_epoch is the adapt-and-EMIT tier the user's directive asks for. Recommending raim without raim_within_epoch does not meet the directive.

★ AUTO-ARM CASCADES (a promotion of one knob silently promotes others): raim_withhold_sigma0>0 => raim_within_epoch (:1542) => raim + raim_attribution (:1555). raim_we_code_iono => raim_within_epoch + raim + raim_attribution (:1574). phase_leveling with no detector => cycle_slip.mw_detect (:1426). ura_retro_bump => emit_clock_disc (:2289). Conversely the loader FORCE-DISABLES: raim_withhold_sigma0 in (0,1] -> 0.0 (:1488); if_phase_td_ref_gate without if_phase_td (:1369); mw_lli_corroborate without mw_detect (:1375); sh_health_gate without estimate_iono_sh or with no active condition (:1665); cb_excursion_reinit with median_m<=0 (:1620).

★ THE SCOPE COUNTEREXAMPLE IN THIS FAMILY is network.sh_health_gate: mechanically correct, arms cleanly, and measured 46.3% of epochs withheld (278/600) with 239 consecutive epochs swallowing both event windows AND the pre-event baseline, because its a00 band is a datum-coupled quantity (invariant #5) that differs ~25 TECU between two realizations of the same day. It is the local analogue of the mw_wl.bridge_sample_debias trap — validated mechanism, non-transferable calibration.

Non-OFF defaults in this family that are nonetheless evidence-backed and should NOT be re-derived: cb_excursion_median_m=50.0 (GnssConfigTypes.hpp:546 — quiet median 0.123 m / 1.4826*MAD 0.071; trips 10 of 2159 epochs; 'anything 20-500 m isolates the same era'); raim_we_code_trigger=10.0 (GnssConfig.hpp:4741 — quiet 2.5-4.7, q99~8, events 17.8-288); if_phase_td_floor_frac=1.0 (sweep 0.5->45 flags, 1.0->26, 1.5->24 — the physical floor binds, k*MAD is dormant on a clean net); if_phase_td_ref_max_consecutive=1 (14->6 at 2, 14->4 at 1); mw_lli_min_epochs=1; raim_surgical_station defaults TRUE already.

CONFIG-HYGIENE GAP found while counting: 16 of 173 carry_invariant configs have NEITHER a pre-fit slip detector (mw_detect / if_phase_td / turbo_edit) NOR carry_invariant_innov_gate. The loader's invariant-#1 auto-arm at :1426 fires only under phase_leveling, so those configs carry stiff phase state with no wired slip response. Worth a separate loader guard; not a knob-default question.

Two named PHANTOM knobs must never be cited or armed in this family (archive_lessons_qc_slip_field.md): network.conditional_raim and network.cycle_slip.prefit_gate are absent from the tree entirely; network.carry_invariant_innov_refold is parsed, warns, and is unimplemented.

Grading discipline that must accompany any promotion run in this family: grade the datum-invariant total_IF(sat) = CLK + 2.545728*CB(sat,C1W) - 1.545728*CB(sat,C2W) as deviation from the per-epoch median over ALL sats INCLUDING the pivot; never rms_clock_m (NetworkStashStatus.cpp:149-155, RMS about zero of the raw clock state, an invariant-#5 violation). Read sigma0_pf_code, never the pooled sigma0_pf (phase post-fit residuals are IDENTICALLY ZERO with free ambiguities). On warm-resume legs judge hourly LEVEL bands, never slopes (ep20 is a local minimum ~30% below the true floor).

(1) emit_pb_filter_gate_v2: 33x / 178x measured improvement, gates G1-G5 all pass, committed armed - yet only 15 of 180 emit_pb_filter configs arm it, and 160 still carry the v1 hand-tunings (jump_k=8, meas_sigma_m=0.1) the card explicitly retired. WARM-RESUME FINGERPRINT MEMBERSHIP (NetworkRunContext.cpp:172-307). In the fingerprint, so they CANNOT be A/B'd on a shared snapshot and cannot be flipped mid-chain: phase_leveling, phase_leveling_max_gap_s, emit_ura, emit_clock_disc, emit_generation_id, emitter_staleness_horizon_s, epoch_decimation_n (conditional, edecim= when != 1). THE M4 / URA PAIRING RULE, stated once because it is the load-bearing scope in this family: the producer channels (emit_ura, emit_phase_bias_sigma at :1825-1826, emit_combined_sigma) are all absent-tolerant and OFF-byte-identical, so arming them costs only wire bytes. The HARM is entirely consumer-side: consume_ura + consume_phase_bias_sigma WITHOUT consume_combined_sigma is the measured p50-1759x fresh-satellite deweight cliff. Arm producer channels freely; arm consumer channels only as the validated set.

SCOPE GAPS I could not close from the record. emit_combined_sigma/M4: 50 sta, 40 min, one held-out station, bias-only - no 305-sta leg, and 305 is exactly where the mw_wl.bridge_sample_debias counterexample flipped sign. emit_clock_disc / emit_generation_id: no isolated A/B anywhere - they were validated only as members of the Card-8 brdc_rts service bundle (3 stations, 121 epochs). emitter_staleness_horizon_s: never set by any config in the repo.

GRADING DISCIPLINE that applies to any run proposed above: decisive PB / convergence / sigma-floor grading stays at 30 s (epoch_decimation_n = 1); counters from a run with a different build or thread count are indicative only - every verdict must come from an in-pair comparison, same exe, same knob shape, same n_threads (project_dev300s_tier).

PROMOTION SHORTLIST (the only three I would move today): network.parallel_seam (measured byte-identical + 1.64x at 305, compare PASS at the exact scale where the FP-drift trap appeared, and already true in 181/181 configs that name it); network.trace_section_timers (measured byte-identical A/B, zero-cost OFF path, already true in 240/355 configs, and every perf number on record is unreproducible without it); network.trace_flag_rates + network.trace_epoch_status (structurally O(epochs)/O(1), and they are the only surfaces for epoch disposition and realized-vs-designed QC alpha).

THE ONE TRAP THAT MOST RESEMBLES TONIGHT'S bridge_sample_debias COUNTEREXAMPLE IN THIS FAMILY: network.parallel_carry. It has a standing user directive to arm it everywhere (feedback_allparallel_release_runs.md) AND a doxygen usage rule forbidding graded verdicts from an ON run (GnssConfigTypes.hpp:437-439). Both are correct — the equivalence was MEASURED only for the dev300s/eq34 config family at a fixed thread count. Do not generalize that license to a new config, a new build, or a different n_threads.

(2) parallel_seam / parallel_carry / lane_carry.parallel_components are ALL silently inert when parallel_stations=false or n_sta <= parallel_min_stations (ApplicationNetworkSetup.cpp:862-865) — no warning is emitted for that case. When a detector (MW wide-lane, RINEX LLI, IF-phase TD, wind-up restart) actuates a refloat on a CARRIED arc, the true integer jump is read from the fixture's truth_slips.csv and the carried level is SHIFTED by exactly sum(delta)*lambda instead of freeing the arc; the gap re-entry drain and the T4 attribution erase are deliberately UNCHANGED, so the arm isolates a perfect DETECTOR response. Window = ( max(last_applied_s, LocalCarry::birth_s, now_s - window_s), now_s ]: the latency term is the load-bearing one, birth_s is the hard floor (a T4 erase deletes the entry and the re-harvest already contains the earlier jump), last_applied_s stops a double apply. NOT LocalCarry::last_seen_s -- that is the PREVIOUS epoch's stash time and a zero-q level is not re-set by an intervening solve, so using it read the normal population as false alarms (701 'false-alarm kept' against 88 repaired on a 60-epoch smoke). knobs.scope: SCOPE the pivot-handover response to the constellation whose clock datum actually changed. ON, the skip/clear/suppress applies only to the changed constellation(s) — the SH-VTEC carry skip deliberately stays global (NetworkRunContext.cpp:2153). knobs.interlock: REQUIRES network.scoped_handover_response (the loader DISARMS with a warning otherwise — the transform releases the skip for the CHANGED constellation only, so with the global response still armed every other constellation would keep free-falling and the edge would not be fixed).  INERT under an anchor-free clock datum (clock_datum_sum_to_zero / clock_datum_broadcast_anchored): those realize the gauge with no pivot satellite, so there is no handover seam — the loader disarms there too.  FINGERPRINTED with an ARMED-ONLY token ('sts:1', NetworkRunContext.cpp): every pre-existing snapshot fingerprint is unchanged and OFF stays byte-identical, but an ARMED run is fresh-convergence only — never flip it mid-chain, and an A/B against a stored snapshot is invalid (increment 0 learned this the hard way, section 19.4).  Two responses deliberately NOT released and documented: the NetworkClockQc jump test (its statistic is the RAW clock, which genuinely steps by the datum delta at a handover; the edge stays classified as FRAME) and the two-state clock oscillator (clock_model is a documented NO-GO).  NOT a consumer fix: the switch-epoch disc declarations are UNCHANGED by design, so the consumer still resets at the edge — that is an EMISSION question and the named increment 2 (split the per-satellite disc bump by family so a clock-only re-reference stops resetting ambiguities).
knobs.regime: on("network.scoped_handover_response") and not on("network.clock_datum_sum_to_zero") and not on("network.clock_datum_broadcast_anchored")

Unlike that row there is NO n_sys >= 2 term: the transform acts on the CHANGED constellation's own carry, so a single constellation is enough for it to do work.  It does require scoped_handover_response, because releasing the changed constellation's skip while the global response still invalidates every sibling would not fix the edge.

knobs.scope: COLD ANCHOR-FALLBACK (SPEC_event_harness §15 + §16.8).  The anchor election sweeps the coverage-ranked candidates and takes the FIRST that tracks the key; only AFTERWARDS does the continuous branch look that successor up in the one-epoch handover ledger and apply its usability predicate.  A family whose top-ranked tracker has no usable carried value therefore goes COLD — re-realizing the family's gauge, marking it for re-reference and erasing its leveling carries at every station — while a lower-ranked tracker holding a mature converged arc sits unused (cbscope5 storm arm: 43 of 47 non-cold-start cold handovers had >= 3 mature alternatives, and in NONE was the successor the best-placed candidate).  ON: where a handover is about to happen (an incumbent exists for the key and the sticky branch did not keep it) the sweep gains a FIRST pass over the SAME coverage-ranked list accepting only candidates whose carry is USABLE — the continuous branch's OWN predicate (one shared lambda, two readers), plus 'not itself freed this epoch' (both freed vehicles) and an arc-age bar (network.phase_datum_candidacy_min_age_ep, default 60 loop epochs; 0 = no test, unknown age = mature).  With none usable the election falls through to today's two sweeps unchanged, counted. PROPERTY: handover_cold then counts exactly the UNAVOIDABLE re-realizations.  Two deliberate non-entries: a kept sticky incumbent, and an incumbent-LESS key (a first sighting has no outgoing frame, the continuous branch cannot run for it, and every pin there is a 0-pin whichever station takes it).  ITERATION 2 adds network.phase_datum_candidacy_satellite (default TRUE under this knob): a satellite's families that hand over in the same epoch take ONE successor, and a partial handover prefers the station already anchoring its other families — the per-family screen of iteration 1 let a satellite's three bands elect three hosts.

(1) OFF absorbs the step 100.000 % IN THE EPOCH IT LANDS (+0, not +1), at every size tested - 0.05 m, 0.5 m, 10 m - with a settled residual of 2-31 micrometres, and NOTHING else in the network moves: the station's other arcs 7e-06 to 3.8e-05 cyc (44-220x BELOW the null floor), ZWD <= 3.9e-05 m, slant iono <= 5.4e-05 m, the emitted satellite clocks 1e-06 to 5e-06 m rms, the consumer 0.0000 m.  The receiver clock is a free per-epoch parameter, so a range-direction step at one station is EXACTLY estimable there and leaks nowhere.  (2) ON is WORSE by a scale-linear 0.104 % of the step at the event epoch - absorb_0 0.998962 at ALL THREE sizes (0.5 mm at 0.05 m, 5.2 mm at 0.5 m, 10.4 mm at 10 m) - because the carried prior fights the step with its share of the epoch's normal equations, and the frame reaction grows with it (oth_d rms 3.8e-05 -> 1.76e-04 cyc at 10 m, ZWD peak 3.9e-05 -> 5.0e-03 m, consumer 0.0000 -> -0.0018 m).  Every one of those is still below the null floor, so the honest statement is 'no measurable benefit, a measurable-but-sub-floor cost'.  (3) THE JUMP GATE CANNOT SEE A REALISTIC STEP.  The new armed-only run-end census (k*sqrt(var_pred) in METRES) reads 'k = 10.0 sigma over 3660 station-epoch test(s) => gate mean 7.9863 m, min 3.0261 m, max 300.0161 m' on this seed; the 300 m tail is the documented first-increment case (uninformative rate prior) and removing it puts the SETTLED gate at ~3.1 m.  0.5 m is 6x BELOW the tightest station-epoch and 0.05 m is 60x below, so the pre-registered 'above the gate' arm was unreachable at the default k and both sizes landed in the 'below' arm.  A pre-registered extra pair at 10 m (33 ns - an ordinary receiver-clock jump) reached it: exactly 1 refusal, n_rxclk_carry_refused 0 -> 1, gate tests 3660 -> 3659 (the erased station skips its next test - both edges visible).  (4) AND THE RESPONSE IS ONE EPOCH LATE BY CONSTRUCTION: the refusal fires at HARVEST, after the solve, so the epoch the step lands on has already folded the stale prior - the 10.4 mm leak at +0 happens WITH the refusal armed, and the gate only cleans up from +1.  OPEN, invariant #7: the refusal has a counter but NO identity - no event row, no station, no epoch - so on a field lineage 'N refusals' cannot be attributed to a receiver.

knobs.scope: When the T4 attribution tier erases an ISOLATED-ARC (statistical) cell, free every band EXCEPT the one with the smallest |r/sigma0| and keep that band's carried level pinned (if every band stands above k*sigma0 the pin is the least-BAD band, counted separately).  MECHANISM (docs/SPEC_event_harness.md §9 Study 1, §Z Study 3): freeing all three bands strips the LOS's last level anchor, so (rho, I, N1..3) re-draw from one epoch of code and the arc keeps a ~0.45-cyc level error for the rest of the hour that no post-fit screen can see (0 re-flags); one pinned band keeps the LOS's (range, iono) split anchored and the residual is that of a correctly handled real slip. knobs.scope: When Melbourne-Wübbena pairs flag a satellite at a station, free only the bands the evidence NAMES: a pair that the detector evaluated this epoch, whose arc count is >= network.cycle_slip.common_band_min_arc_epochs (10) and which did NOT flag is SILENT and exonerates both its bands — unless the IF-TD detector flagged that pair this epoch (the equal-count trap: L1 and L2 slipping by the same integer leave MW(1,2) silent but move the iono-free combination 0.107 m per cycle) — and a band with a loss-of-lock flag is always implicated.  Implicated = bands no silent pair vouches for; one verdict per (station, satellite, epoch) governs every drain (MW refloat, LLI free, IF-TD pair refloat), so the per-epoch union is exactly the implicated set.  ANCHOR CLAUSE: on an arc that anchors ANY family of the satellite the verdict never narrows (reason anchor_colocate; all bands freed so the satellite's families move together to one successor).  Fallbacks to today's all-band response: no pair fired, nothing exonerated, or an inconsistent verdict (a fired pair whose bands are all exonerated).  MECHANISM (docs/SPEC_event_harness.md §14): a single-band slip fires every pair containing the band, and the drain refloats each firing pair's two bands, so the union is all three — the §9 all-band floor (0.45–0.65 cyc for 45 epochs at low elevation, slant iono −0.08 m) for a one-band event; on the storm bed ~2.2 admissions per detection row, i.e. most responses were all-band.  RULE F2 (the LLI shadow, s14.11): a pair whose band carried a receiver flag at the previous epoch is IMMATURE for the verdict (the MW detector withholds the flagged epoch's sample and keeps the arc, so the lane's next silence is judged against statistics that swallowed the slip); basis token lli_shadow(n=), counter cb_lli_shadow.  RULE F3 (the LLI-epoch verdict, s14.12): at a receiver-flagged epoch where no MW pair flagged, the verdict is formed from the receiver's bits (implicated = the flagged bands, no exoneration step; basis lli=;mw=withheld; counters cb_lli_verdicts / cb_lli_narrowed) so every drain at that epoch -- the LLI drain and every IF-TD pair drain -- frees only the flagged band; T1_if_slip rows carry cb_kept=<bands> when a verdict refused a band. knobs.scope: SIM-ONLY DIAGNOSTIC, the second axis of the ORACLE 2x2 (network.cycle_slip.oracle_relevel's row is the first).  'repair' is the default and is s13.5's ceiling - shift the carried level by the true sum(delta)*lambda read from the fixture's truth_slips.csv.  'free' DECLINES the oracle for true slips: the caller runs today's ordinary free / re-level for that arc.  Paired with oracle_false_alarm = 'keep' it isolates exactly one population - actuations with NO truth slip in the window keep their level, every real slip pays the shipped response - which separates 'the detectors' false alarms are a material injection source' from 'the true-slip re-level is the whole lever'.  The fourth corner (both 'free') is a pure no-op and is the byte-identity control for the hook itself; the loader WARNs rather than refuses so it can be run as that control.  The false-alarm keeps are also split PER TIER in the run-end counters, which is what makes the arm attributable.
knobs.regime_why: It is a policy field of the oracle; without oracle_relevel there is no oracle to steer.  The oracle itself is warn-and-DISARMed off the phase-leveling vehicle and under carry_invariant.

THE ARM, runs/golden_sim_campaign_zwdblk_orafa (true_slip 'free' + false_alarm 'keep' on the in-block posture, vs runs/golden_sim_campaign_zwdblk): 6804 false alarms KEPT (MW 4156 / IF-TD 2131 / LLI 517), 3409 true slips freed as today. FAIL.  ** THE FINDING: the false-alarm re-levels are a RESYNC mechanism.**  NOT re-levelling an arc that had no slip makes the consumer 2.7x worse and forces 62 % more erases, so on this bed the detectors' 50 % false-alarm rate is doing useful work by accident - dragging drifting arcs back into their station's current (walking) frame.  ** WHAT THIS CLOSES: 'tighten the detector thresholds on this bed' is dead as a card** (a better detector removes the resyncs and leaves the walk), and with s6.17b (T4 mostly re-erases the damage its own previous re-level created) BOTH accuracy-of-response levers are now measured - the response's ACCURACY is not what the consumer buys from it.  ** COUNTING BASIS, never to be mixed in a rate: the census counts EVENTS per (station, satellite) (~2300 false per 6 h); the oracle counters count per-signal ACTUATIONS (6804); the retired '13485 actuations' figure was the per-signal OFFER count.**  Rider: this false-alarm rate is a property of THIS BED - the fixture's phase noise is ~5x the field's while the MW thresholds are field-empirical (s6.14.3, feedback_mw_thresholds_empirical), so a fixed physical threshold does not port; the same probe on the field is unowned.

knobs.knob: network.ambiguity_resolution.trace  (the Phase-2 producer-AR diagnostic's per-DD trace)
knobs.scope: TRACE-CLASS and READ-ONLY.  With network.ambiguity_resolution.enable armed, NetworkProducerAr forms between-station double differences of the network's float ambiguities (star topology per (constellation, signal): one reference satellite, one reference station), builds their conditional covariance and runs MLAMBDA on the ils_max_dim lowest-sigma of them.  Phase 2 does NOT re-pin and does NOT re-solve, so the emitted product is byte-identical to the unarmed run; this knob adds logs/network_producer_ar.csv - ONE ROW PER DD OF THE WHOLE BASIS, not just the searched subset, because the fixability CEILING is a statement about the population the ils_max_dim cap chose FROM.  Columns: week,tow,cons,signal,sat_j,ref_sat,sta_r,ref_sta,lambda_m,float_cyc,sigma_cyc,in_subset,fixed_int,kept,ratio,p_succ,n_dd,n_search,n_fixed.  Graded by scripts/simnet_producer_ar_grade.py against the simulator's per-station truth (simnet_amb_integer.load_truth / n_at).
knobs.regime_why: The trace writes rows the search produces; without .enable there is no search and the loader warns.

knobs.interlock: Requires network.ambiguity_resolution.enable (loader warns and writes nothing otherwise).  READ-ONLY: Phase 2 does not re-pin and does not re-solve, so the emitted product is byte-identical to the unarmed run - but .enable's SEARCH is not free, so this pair is never a field or production posture.  ** The trace is only interpretable against TRUTH** (scripts/simnet_producer_ar_grade.py joins simnet_amb_integer.load_truth / n_at); on a field lineage it writes rows nobody can grade.  Provenance keys ambiguity_resolution.{enable,trace,ils_max_dim} join the manifest only when armed, so an unarmed manifest's bytes are unchanged.  ** Two indexing traps the implementation already handles and any reader must respect: IlsResult::kept indexes the CAPPED, sigma-PERMUTED search vector while afix is in kept order** - netar::mapFixToBasis does the double indirection and is unit-tested (tests/test_producer_ar_trace.cpp) with the naive mapping as an explicit negative control, because getting it wrong yields a well-formed CSV with the integers on the wrong satellites and nothing downstream can tell.  ** And the file's DDs share ONE reference pair per (constellation, signal)**, which rotates - 213 / 261 reference-satellite and 242 / 313 reference-station switches over 2869 epochs on the first arm - so any per-band or per-station split off this trace compares rotating populations (s6.12).  The run-end clause carries invariant-#4 branches for 'armed but the ILS ran on zero epochs' and 'trace armed but zero rows', plus a WARN whenever a fix is accepted on a carry-BLIND covariance - which is the warning that fired throughout the first arm.
